diagnostic_evidence.quote: While not identical to classical Chebyshev points, such nodes exhibit the same characteristic clustering near the interval endpoints. It is a well-established result in approximation theory that the Lebesgue constant for polynomial interpolation at these nodes exhibits logarithmic growth
\ell_j(\theta) = \frac{\sin(\theta)}{\sin(\theta_j)} \frac{\prod_{k \ne j} \left( \cos\theta - \cos\theta_k \right)}{\prod_{k \ne j} \left( \cos\theta_j - \cos\theta_k \right)}.

issues.failure_explanation: For fixed δ>0, the angles occupy [a,π-a] with a>0, where the derivative of cos is bounded away from zero. The transformed nodes therefore have endpoint spacing of order 1/N, not Chebyshev endpoint clustering. The product formula gives a concrete contradiction: take δ=L, so sin θ≥√3/2. At the midpoint of the first uniform-grid interval, a central cardinal function is bounded below by (√3/2)^N times the corresponding equispaced-polynomial cardinal function. The latter has magnitude of order 2^N/N², giving Λ_N≥c(√3)^N/N².

failure_location.quote: For any fixed extension $\delta > 0$, the growth is logarithmic.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Abandon the logarithmic bound for these grids, or construct genuinely endpoint-clustered physical nodes and reanalyze that different discretization.
issues.overall_effect: The logarithmic one-dimensional bound and its O((log N)^d) tensor-product consequence fail on the stated uniform physical grids.
issues.title: Cosines of angles restricted away from 0 and π are not logarithmically stable Chebyshev nodes
issues.why_classification: The claimed logarithmic rate is contradicted by exponential growth in an allowed fixed-extension regime. Preserving logarithmic stability requires changing the advertised uniform-grid method.

issues.failure_explanation: The inverse matrix is only one factor in the interpolation operator; near-degeneracy of a basis can be canceled by its evaluation functions. For fixed distinct nodes and fixed N, Λ_N therefore tends to the finite ordinary-polynomial interpolation Lebesgue constant.
